poems.title: Out of Life
poems.sub: the maze, the haze, the fall, the ember
poems.fx_name: Breath on the Window & Rising Fire-Escape Embers
poems.afterlight_ref: Air A5 (Breath on the Glass) + A1 (Fog by Depth) + 09 (Picture to Embers to Stars)
poems.idea: Condensation fogs the far depth planes while the near figure clears the glass; falling out of life sheds upward-streaking embers.
poems.picture: Each Common Place (The Underpass Shadow-Pool, The Severn's Spiral Escape, The Orange Catwalk) breathes condensation across the glass by estimated depth. Where the actor moves in the foreground, the glass clears; along the fire escape, high-luminance points lift off as cyan and amber bokeh embers.
poems.sound: Malhun in Bayati mode over the suite master audio (0:00–2:03), with sub-bass drone steps.
poems.code: Depth-weighted condensation envelope from depth_sharp.npz + curl-noise advected bokeh embers spawned from real scene highlights.
poems.after: “The vape gathers, inside and out. My vision blurs. I move toward the window — and you only get further away… You fall off the fire escape, into darkness — and the city streaks upward.”

What we've made we don't want, what we've sold to the world, to ourselves, doesn't exist.
I look for a way out through the hallways, within the drawers and fire escapes,
trip on my own words, falling out of life, and find where you go when you leave.
The vape gathers, inside and out. My vision blurs. I move toward the window — and you only get further away. More haze.

It was the maze constructed by a tainted love, a known yet unknown pit beneath the quicksands of the make -believe haven, and hidden in
the overnourished forest of escapism that calls for you. At this age, I'll follow, following the full distance between us almost having it all and
starting anew, to rediscover when love was real. I failed at protecting you from your own vices,

dripping blood salivating on imminent doubts, fully awakening to our darkest nights.

I trip on my own words, falling out of life — and find where you go when you leave. The gap between us breathes, and never closes.

poems.title: How to break off an engagement
poems.sub: the storm takes everything that was ever called goods
poems.fx_name: Refracting Raindrop Lenses, Wet Time-Rivulet & Mud Relief
poems.afterlight_ref: Dew 02c/02d (Pane & Worms: drops leave wet tracks that keep playing) + Matter M4 (Mud, by outline)
poems.idea: Falling raindrops act as true physical water-dome lenses whose wet rivulets replay the moment the drop passed; storm aftermath presses outlines into wet stone relief.
poems.picture: Across the Drowned Atrium and chapel rose window, organic teardrop water lenses slide down the glass. Each droplet refracts the underlying cel plate by Snell's law (∂H/∂x, ∂H/∂y) with a natural upper-left Fresnel crescent and leaves a wet rivulet running the delayed frame from when the drop passed.
poems.sound: Dirge in pentatonic mode; thunder, tambourine echoes off empty choir stands, and rain on stone.
poems.code: Continuous 2D water-heightfield H(x,y) normal refraction (cv2.remap) + temporal rivulet trail buffer + Sobel depth-contour relief (M4 Mud).
poems.after: “It thunders. Then rains until nothing remains… Ode to two sets of mud-imprinted footsteps, leading away from what the water kept.”

poems.title: Nevermore
poems.sub: a trail followed twice, a vow made twice
poems.fx_name: Darkroom Silver-Gelatin Tray & Two-Block Linocut Memory

poems.idea: A print develops in a sloshing darkroom tray: deep selenium-silver ink for now, burnished gold leaf for what the picture just let go.
poems.picture: The Named Viaduct and Shore Steps develop like a silver-gelatin print under a gentle liquid tray wave. Carved over the silver plate is a two-block linocut: deep indigo-silver holds the present posture, while burnished gold ink (#e88f0e) prints the temporal delta of what just moved.
poems.sound: Suite movement IV over Mirror Thread Bay's low tide and muted wind.
poems.code: Selenium silver-gelatin tonal curve + sinusoidal developer-tray refraction + temporal motion-delta gold woodblock relief overlay.
poems.after: “A trail followed twice, a vow made twice… The plants in a golden hue bloom, and face toward me in anticipation… The clouds mute the stars for the deepest level of darkness.”

At the end of each station, the 35mm frame catches in the projector gate and burns open with a white-gold core and scarlet-poppy halation.

poems.code: Background curl-noise fluid marbling (cv2.remap) + dual Keplerian orbital light pools + 3-stage 35mm celluloid gate-burn (core/amber/char).
